components: elongated swad-series oval with a short tooth
strokeOrder: close the elongated upper oval clockwise and finish its short tooth
after one lift, restart below the oval and sweep through the lower bowl from right to left
after another lift, place the dot above last

strokeOrderSource.variation: The independent-form animations build the elongated swad-series body before its upper dot: the upper oval closes clockwise and finishes with its short tooth, the pen restarts for the lower right-to-left bowl, and the dot is placed last after a second lift. The adjacent prose distinguishes zwad from fe by its elongated body and tooth, while the chapter identifies zwad as the dotted member of the swad series. This three-run learner path fits those movements to the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback. The evidence and glyph identity remain Urdu-specific rather than borrowing Arabic ض's independently sourced order.

notes: Primarily appears in words of Arabic origin; homophonous with Urdu ze and zal in ordinary pronunciation.
